source: Native AWS DynamoDB ExecuteStatement via scripts/aws/aws_cli.py; no DynamoDB Local observations included
notes: Requests and outputs are AWS CLI JSON, not raw HTTP bytes. Native errors retain modeled fields. CLI retries were bounded to two attempts and each CLI process to 45 seconds.
Call 91 is AWS CLI ParamValidation before transport, not a native AWS response. Call 25 is a PartiQL syntax rejection for unquoted missing, not evidence about projecting an absent attribute.
LastEvaluatedKey and NextToken absence is preserved verbatim; null placeholders were not added to captured outputs.
No production source, existing captures, builds, tests, linters or formatters were modified or run.

nativeFacts.fact: Ascending single-partition pages returned physical pk and sk in LastEvaluatedKey independently of projection. Limit applied to evaluated items: filtered empty pages still returned both continuation fields. Observed final ascending A pages omitted both fields, including Limit equal to the four-item count.

Continuation fields are not interchangeable. The exact pk+sk Limit=1 query returned LastEvaluatedKey but no NextToken. Descending A at its final item and fan-out B at its final item with Limit=1 still returned both fields, then an empty terminal page omitted both. Do not infer exhaustion solely from result count or universally require an extra empty page.

Partition-key IN fan-out paged the A partition before B in these requests. At the observed A-to-B operation boundary, NextToken was present while LastEvaluatedKey was absent, including projected and fully filtered pages. Within a partition LastEvaluatedKey identified its physical table key. No claim is made that operand order determines every fan-out execution order.

Unkeyed table SELECT paging returned table pk/sk. GSI SELECT paging returned all four physical table/index key attributes pk, sk, gp and gs in LastEvaluatedKey even when none were projected, and on empty filtered pages. Terminal GSI pages omitted both continuation fields.

Reusing a native token with the same request succeeded. Changed Limit, omitted Limit and changed ConsistentRead succeeded. Changed projection, whitespace, order, filter, table-to-index statement or partition parameter values failed ValidationException: NextToken does not match request. Reversing the IN parameter order also failed with that message.

Plain junk, base64 empty object, a locally shaped opIndexToExclusiveNextKey object, truncated native token and a mutated native token failed native ValidationException: Invalid NextToken. The locally shaped object is only malformed input sent to AWS, not output from a DynamoDB Local experiment.
The unique owned table and its GSI were deleted. DescribeTable subsequently returned ResourceNotFoundException, verifying absence.

uncertainties: No 1-MB boundary, large fan-out, token expiry, cross-account/cross-region token reuse, concurrent item mutation, throttling, LSI, binary/numeric key or GSI non-ALL projection experiment was performed.

Observed exhaustion and fan-out operation boundaries may depend on native execution/storage choices. This small capture supports field independence and physical-key provenance, not a universal deterministic last-page lookahead algorithm.
Only a fresh seven-item table with two partitions and one GSI was measured. No production resource was queried or changed.
Pinned DynamoDB Local 3.3.1 comparison was not run in this assignment; native observations must not be represented as local behavior.
